steps.title: Load a water utility
steps.say: An invented utility: 40 districts, 20,000 junctions, about 33,600 pipes, ten years of recorded pipe failures, and two weeks of pressure and flow readings every 15 minutes. Somewhere in it are a leak, a sensor that is going wrong, and a night of heavy but harmless water use.

steps.title: Find what is unusual, and say what it is
steps.say: Every district is checked. Night flow is compared with what that district's days normally imply, so a simply busy day does not raise an alarm. Three districts stand out, and each gets a different verdict.

steps.title: Where is the leak?
steps.say: A leak lowers pressure most near itself. For each of the district's 500 junctions the hydraulic model predicts the pattern of pressure drops a leak there would cause at the ten sensors; the junction whose pattern fits best is the answer. Then the model is asked directly: what would a leak of that size there do?

steps.title: Two alarms that are not leaks
steps.say: One pressure sensor reads lower every day, but no extra water is entering the district and its neighbours are steady: the sensor is at fault, not the pipes. In another district the flow jumped for one night and went back: a leak does not repair itself.

steps.title: Send a crew, to the right places only
steps.say: The leak gets an urgent work order with a small area to survey. The sensor gets a routine recalibration, no digging. The harmless night of demand is refused a work order.

body.note: Night flow up for four nights. Acoustic survey from the best candidate outwards.

steps.title: Which pipes will break next?
steps.say: A model learns from failures up to 2022 and is tested on 2023 to 2025, which it never saw. It is compared with the rule most utilities start from: the oldest pipes are the riskiest.

steps.title: Five years of replacements on a fixed budget
steps.say: With $4 million a year, which pipes should be replaced and when? The plan ranks pipes by failure cost avoided per dollar, and is set beside replacing the oldest pipes first with the same money.

steps.title: The audit trail
steps.say: Who loaded the network, what was detected, who sent crews and who set the plan: recorded in a log that cannot be edited.
